ai.title: Blue Planet III is keeping the rough edges in the age of AI
ai.brief: BBC’s Blue Planet III is keeping in shots that would normally end up on the cutting room floor to prove it’s real. BBC’s Blue Planet III is keeping in shots that would normally end up on the cutting room floor to prove it’s real. BBC’s Blue Planet III is looking to prove its authenticity by leaving in the less-than-perfect shots. Previous incarnations of the nature series were defined by their gorgeous, crystal-clear footage that seemed almost too good to be real. But one dead giveaway of AI is when things look too polished and seamless. To counter that, Blue Planet III goes warts and all. Executive Producer Elizabeth White told The Guardian in the past, “the amount of plankton and things” floating in the water would have caused them to cut a shot.
